clue.text: Out of bed and very tired, but cheerful

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
dead beat, or simply beat, means exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone up and about despite exhaustion still manages to be in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: An upbeat mood is an optimistic, positive one, so the adjective is a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Remaining in shop getting book exchanged for second not requested

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and a different letter put in its place

parts.note: goods still in the shop have not been bought

explanation.surface: Stock left on the shelves gets swapped for something else that nobody asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged for' swaps the B of UNBOUGHT for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsought was never looked for or asked for, a direct synonym of not requested.

clue.text: Boringly characterless group's left in second place

indicators.note: the letter is slotted in as the second letter of the other word

parts.note: a band is a musical group; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A band's departing member is described as dull and uninspiring, coming second.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland food or people lack any strong flavour or personality, so the word means dull and characterless.

clue.text: Beer, light with no head

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a pale colour is a light one

explanation.surface: A pale beer is served without a frothy head on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer brewed with top-fermenting yeast.

clue.text: What Rose working will do to be tiresome as a temp?

parts.note: what an anagram of ROSE does to the word tiresome is to separate, or part, from it

indicators.note: Rose is worked, its letters rearranged, so it can be found within and removed from the longer word

parts.note: the word as written, supplying the letter pool
the name taken as letters to be removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose finds her temporary job dull and wearisome.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks what ROSE, rearranged ('working'), will do to 'tiresome': it will part from it, leaving TIME. So the answer is PART plus TIME. An unusual, whimsical construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp works part-time hours, or on a temporary basis, so 'as a temp' describes part-time work.

clue.text: Collection of weapons favoured by some football supporters

definitions.meaning: a store of arms and ammunition
the name of a famous north London football club, followed by many fans

explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a weapons store, and Arsenal is a Premier League football club in London.

clue.text: Subversive act ultimately fair

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of the word

parts.note: a fair price or judgment is a reasonable one

explanation.surface: A rebellious deed is deemed, in the end, to be justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasonable conduct betrays or undermines the state, so it is subversive in a strong sense.

clue.text: International time I introduced to the French, among other things

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: one letter is introduced into, placed inside, the other word

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: An international period sees a figure introduced to French society, among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is the Latin phrase meaning among other things, used in formal English.

clue.text: Queen has to speak angrily so some knights are called

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for the Queen
to rant is to speak loudly and angrily

explanation.surface: The monarch must vent her anger so that certain knights are summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Knights errant were knights who wandered in search of adventure; the definition is the phrase describing that title. 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval wandering knights were known as knights errant, so the word is how some knights are described.

clue.text: One who objects loses argument in favour of one experimenting

indicators.note: the longer word drops the shorter word from within it

parts.note: a protester objects to something
a pro is an argument for something, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A protester drops a supporting argument in favour of someone running trials.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester tries things out, so a tester is someone experimenting or trialling.

clue.text: Quite brazen, offering fake drug in smaller quantity

parts.note: a sham is a fake or imitation
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Someone peddling counterfeit drugs in reduced amounts is utterly brazen.
explanation.definitionFit: A shameless person has no sense of shame, so the word is a synonym of brazen.

clue.text: Go into heart of America? Conservative's not in it

indicators.note: the letter is not in the word, so it is removed

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, meaning heart
C is the abbreviation for Conservative; 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Travelling into America's heartland is a place where conservatives are absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of America' asks for the American spelling CENTER, not the middle letters of America.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is to go into it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Appreciates where to find supporters for football crowds

definitions.text: where to find supporters for football crowds
definitions.meaning: the structural supports holding up the stands where football fans sit are beneath them

explanation.definitionFit: To understand something is to appreciate it, and the beams supporting grandstands are under the stands.

clue.text: Heavy footwear has girl going under the waves

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece is placed below the other

parts.note: rollers are long heavy waves
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Wearing heavy boots, a girl called Kate goes under the breaking waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word; 'going under' puts KATE below ROLLERS in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller skate is a boot or shoe fitted with wheels, fairly heavy footwear, so the phrase is a playful description.

clue.text: Managed to get king off row of squares

indicators.note: the letter is taken off the word

parts.note: in chess, a rank is a horizontal row of squares
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player manages to move the king off a row of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface is apt: a rank is a row of the board and K stands for king.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it, so ran is the past tense equivalent of managed.

clue.text: One seeking to stem flow in piping up from the floor

definitions.text: One seeking to stem flow in piping up from the floor

parts.words: One seeking to stem flow in piping up from the floor
parts.note: sounds like a plumber blocking a pipe rising from the floor, but describes an audience member interrupting a speaker's flow with shouts

explanation.definitionFit: Hecklers shout interruptions from the audience to disrupt a speaker's flow of words.

clue.text: Frozen channel of Sussex river just below hilltop

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits immediately under the first

parts.note: a crest is the top of a hill
the Arun is a river in the English county of West Sussex

explanation.surface: A river in Sussex flows just beneath the summit of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cresta Run is the famous ice toboggan track at St Moritz in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cresta Run is a natural ice skeleton-toboggan run, literally a frozen channel.

clue.text: In trial, one lying is without friends

indicators.note: the answer is held within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: During a court trial, a witness who lies finds themselves isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: A lonely person is isolated and without company or friends.

clue.text: Irritates son? That's uncalled for

parts.note: to needle someone is to irritate them

explanation.surface: Annoying one's son is said to be unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, so it is synonymous with uncalled for.

clue.text: Calm seen around about the Queen

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes around the other piece
about indicates the letters of seen are turned about, rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen is seen looking composed as she moves around.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators sit side by side: 'about' scrambles 'seen' into SENE, and 'around' wraps that round the royal initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A serene person is calm and untroubled, a close synonym.

clue.text: Strong desire, say, to send up top-selling book

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending up means reading the letters upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the top-selling item is the No 1, written NO I
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Wanting badly to mock a bestseller.
explanation.walkthrough: NO I TOME, the number one book, read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire is an example of a feeling, so 'say' marks it as one instance of the answer.

clue.text: Pioneer of computers that made a lot of notes

definitions.meaning: Charles, the Victorian mathematician who designed the first mechanical computer

definitions.text: that made a lot of notes
definitions.meaning: the name is spelt entirely with musical note letters A to G

explanation.definitionFit: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine, and every letter of his surname is a musical note.

clue.text: No time to cry over card game

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the whole sequence is turned upside down

parts.note: taken as written
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: No time to weep about a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + T + SOB, read upwards ('over'), gives BOS TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is an old card game related to whist.

clue.text: Sign of hesitation after Washington representative gives money to US natives

indicators.note: the hesitation sound comes after the other pieces

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A Washington politician, umming and erring, gives cash to Native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Wampum was strings of shell beads used as currency by Native American peoples.

clue.text: Even pieces of carpet may be appropriate

indicators.note: take the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Evenly cut lengths of carpet may suit the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or fitting, a synonym of appropriate.

clue.text: An end of his — we stop hard work?

definitions.text: An end of his — we stop hard work?

indicators.note: take one end, here the final letter, of the word
the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A union official declares the end of hard work by calling a stoppage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a union representative who might call a halt to hard work, while S from 'his' with WE STOP HARD rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop steward is a union official in a workplace who may call members out on strike.

clue.text: Emerged from a garden sprinkler

parts.note: the rose is the perforated nozzle on a watering can

explanation.surface: Something appeared from the spray of a garden watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning came up or emerged.

clue.text: Going over a chart showing river within Italian city

indicators.note: the assembled letters are turned over, reversed
the river letter sits inside the chart

parts.note: a map is a chart

explanation.surface: Reading a chart that shows a river flowing through an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: A + MAP around R gives AMRAP, which 'Going over' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in northern Italy, famous for ham and cheese.

clue.text: Pottery with smooth and singular quality of hue

parts.note: to iron clothes is to smooth them
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tone is a shade or quality of colour

explanation.surface: Ceramics with a smooth finish and a distinctive colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone china is a hard, durable kind of earthenware, a type of pottery.

clue.text: Hardened group usually found together

definitions.meaning: become firm, as jelly or concrete does
a collection of things belonging together

explanation.definitionFit: Jelly that has set has hardened, and a set is a group of matching items.

clue.text: One who painted sheep in a pronounced style

indicators.note: the sheep goes inside the other piece
the word for style is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: manner means style or way of doing something
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: An artist painted a sheep in a distinctive style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' works because in standard British speech the final R of the word for style is silent, so it sounds like the food from heaven. Andrea Mantegna was an Italian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Mantegna was a fifteenth-century Italian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: He leaves pagan's city in Greece

indicators.note: the letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: a heathen is a pagan; the possessive keeps its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man abandons the city of a pagan in ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATHEN'S loses HE to leave ATHEN'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital and largest city of Greece.
